note: Adapted from the original English description in Snyder 1924, where the species is described as Rhinotermes longidens, new species, with large and small soldiers distinguished and a set of measurements given for each (large soldier pl. X fig. 1, small soldier fig. 2); the alate and worker are not described. The original records neither type locality nor collection data (the paper is titled "An extraordinary new Rhinotermes from Panama"); a footnote states that the account of R. longilabius is by A. Emerson of the University of Pittsburgh, and the comparison cited in this entry comes from the account referred to in that footnote.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Smaller than R. longilabius Emerson from British Guiana, but with longer mandibles, larger marginal teeth, a narrower labrum and a smaller pronotum; the upper marginal tooth of the right mandible is larger and parallel to the mandibular margin; antennae 15-segmented, against 16 in longilabius. Only 3 species of large American soldiers with a long labrum are known; besides the two above there is R. intermedius Snyder from Bolivia.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: head straw-yellow, labrum yellowish brown, mandibles yellow at the base and chestnut brown at the tip. Front of head narrow, behind rounded, with scattered long hairs; labrum slender and long, widest at the base; mandibles slender, long and sharp, curved inwards, with prominent marginal teeth; antennae 15-segmented, white tinged with yellow, the 3rd segment slender, subclavate, shorter than the 2nd and longer than the 4th; pronotum saddle-shaped, posterior margin nearly straight, anterior margin raised; legs white, slender, hairy; abdomen pale straw-yellow, cerci prominent. Measurements: total length 3.60 mm; head with mandibles 1.65 mm; head without mandibles (to the front) 1.00 mm; left mandible length 0.80 mm; labrum length 0.60 mm; pronotum length 0.27 mm; hind tibia 0.76 mm; head width (at the widest point) 1.00 mm; labrum width at the tip 0.15 mm, at the base 0.22 mm, mean width at the middle 0.15 mm; pronotum width 0.55 mm. Small soldier: head pale straw-yellow, paler behind, widest at the posterior margin, conical at the front; labrum slender and long, slightly constricted at the base, forked at the tip, each fork with a long hair; mandibles degenerate at the tip, almost invisible; antennae 14-segmented, the 3rd segment subclavate, longer than the 2nd and 4th; pronotum pale yellow, saddle-shaped, posterior margin slightly concave; legs white tinged with yellow, slender, with long hairs; abdomen pale yellow, each tergite with a row of long hairs at the base, cerci prominent. Measurements: total length 2.20—2.40 mm; head with labrum 1.05 mm; head without labrum 0.57 mm; labrum length 0.50 mm; pronotum length 0.22 mm; hind tibia 0.57—0.60 mm.
